Simulate a population

Source: R/sim.R
pmx_ode_sim.Rd

Draws each subject's etas from a multivariate normal with covariance omega, solves every subject at theta and its etas with pmx_ode_solve(), and adds residual error to the outputs sigma names. Every draw is made in R with R's random number generator, so set.seed() makes a simulation reproducible, at any thread count.

Usage

pmx_ode_sim(
  model,
  events,
  theta = double(),
  omega = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  n = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A model from pmx_ode_model().

events

An event table: from pmx_ode_events(), or a NONMEM-style data frame with columns ID, TIME, EVID, AMT, CMT, RATE, DUR, II, ADDL and SS (any case; all but TIME optional). With no EVID, a record with an AMT above 0 is a dose, one with MDV 1 marks a time (EVID 2), and the rest are observations; given EVID, MDV is not read. CMT is a compartment's name or number. Columns named like a model parameter are covariates, each record carrying its value; other columns, such as DV, are ignored.

theta

The model's fixed parameters, a named numeric vector.

omega

The covariance of the etas: a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix, or a named vector of variances for a diagonal one. Its names, or with none the model's parameters whose names start with eta, in the order the model uses them, say which parameters are etas. NULL draws none.

sigma

Residual error: a named list of error models, from add(), prop() or lnorm(), each name a compartment or an output of the model. NULL adds none.

n

The number of subjects. A table of one subject is copied n times, the copies numbered 1 to n; a table of several subjects is simulated once per subject, and n, if given, must be their number.

Value

A data frame with pmx_ode_solve()'s columns, then one column per eta holding the subject's draw, then, for each entry of sigma, the output with residual error, named after it with _obs appended.

Details

The draws are made in a fixed order: first the etas, as MASS::mvrnorm(n, 0, omega) would draw them, one row per subject; then, for each entry of sigma in turn, one standard normal per observation record. A subject the solver fails for still takes its draws, so the others' are unchanged.

Four residual error models are built in: add(), prop(), their sum add(a) + prop(b) (the combined model) and lnorm(). Any other is a function applied to the predictions this returns.

Errors

pmx_ode_error_argument for an argument that is not what is described here; the errors of pmx_ode_solve().

See also

add() for the error models.

Examples

m <- pmx_ode_model({
  ka <- exp(tka); cl <- exp(tcl + eta.cl); v <- exp(tv + eta.v)
  cp <- linCmt()
})
ev <- pmx_ode_events(amt = 100, cmt = "depot", time = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24))
set.seed(1)
sim <- pmx_ode_sim(m, ev, theta = c(tka = 0.5, tcl = 1, tv = 3),
                   omega = diag(c(0.1, 0.1)), sigma = list(cp = prop(0.1)),
                   n = 10)
head(sim)
